A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from AniX to CustomX. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and visual examples, support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation evaluations, action-control and character-consistency results, ablations, hybrid-data experiments and inference measurements in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 reports the retained original experiments and additional latency analyses and qualitative results, including generation within a reconstructed real-world scene.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, flow-matching objective, multimodal conditioning, LoRA training, autoregressive generation and DMD2 acceleration remain unchanged. Renaming the framework and describing shared inference anchors as propagated anchors do not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 and Figure A5 add an actual qualitative test in a reconstructed real-world 3DGS scene. The GTA-V training, 400 real-world training videos, novel-action evaluations and real-character experiments were already present in v1, including its appendix.

E2.justification: Appendix B.5 newly includes HunyuanCustom-13B and Wan2.2-14B in the high-resolution runtime discussion with reported timings; v1's corresponding discussion reported only its own model's cost. The comparator membership in the main quality and control evaluations, Tables 1 and 2, is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendices B.4-B.5 add cold-start timing that includes scene creation and rendering, plus specified 96-frame runtime settings. These extend the evaluation protocol rather than replace the retained 93-frame latency tests. Main benchmark metrics, sample counts and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a second qualitative example to the hybrid-training comparison, a reconstructed-scene case study, and startup/high-resolution cost analyses. The underlying hybrid-data study and multi-view, anchor and long-horizon ablations already existed in v1; moving them or summarizing them in the main text is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and retain ten evaluations using different characters for the long-horizon analysis. V2 explicitly describes ten clips per trial, but adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and v1 Table 5/v2 Table A1 retain identical values. New results include approximately 300/9 seconds for Marble/FlashWorld scene creation, 0.695 seconds for rendering, and 151/182 seconds for HunyuanCustom/Wan2.2 at 720P, plus additional qualitative examples. The new 96-frame timing contexts do not establish improvements over the retained 93-frame measurements.

T1.justification: The conditional generation formulation, flow-matching loss, shifted positional embedding equation and autoregressive token partition are unchanged. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central capability and performance claims remain unchanged. However, v2 Section 4.2 adds an explicit priority claim that this is the first framework jointly integrating 3D or multi-view characters, action prompts, scenes and long-horizon generation; v1 did not explicitly assert this priority.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges non-real-time inference and the inability to handle multiple simultaneously active characters. It also explains differing baseline input configurations, separates one-time scene creation from recurring generation costs, and discusses high-resolution computational limits. These add substantive qualifications to the retained findings.

D1.justification: V2 more explicitly documents anchor handling and ten clips per long-horizon trial, and adds timing hardware and token-workload details. It updates the project-page address but omits the direct CLIP-aesthetic implementation URL retained in v1's bibliography. The principal training and distillation recipes remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Seedance 2.0, FlashWorld and Advancing Open-Source World Models, while removing references including Sora, Magica 2, Edify3D and Meta 3D Gen. It also adds the explicit joint-integration priority claim. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and method name, flattens the method subsection hierarchy, introduces an Experimental Settings subsection, subdivides the appendix, and adds localized explanations and limitations. Most of the scientific narrative remains closely matched rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The paper is extensively reformatted from two columns to one, with resized and relocated tables and figures. Figure 4 becomes a horizontal pipeline, the long-horizon plot is redesigned, and qualitative panels are rearranged. V2 Figure 6 reuses part of v1 Figure 14; Figure A5 and the additional hybrid-training example provide new visual content.

improvement.justification: The added latency accounting in Appendices B.4-B.5 and explicit single-subject/non-real-time limitations improve practical transparency. Figure A5 supplies limited evidence for previously claimed real-world applicability. These are modest gains: the method and principal results remain unchanged, and the new 96-frame timing contexts are not directly comparable with the retained 93-frame measurements.
